category_title: Elementary students with ADHD and language delay who improve concentration and social helpfulness through virtual games
minimal_context: The student is using a computer mouse to click on a single OK bandage in a 3D virtual health center to complete a learning mission.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's complete the learning mission. Use the mouse to click on the single OK bandage in the health center.

STUDENT: (Struggles to smoothly control the mouse to click the virtual object) How many questions are left to answer?

TUTOR: We still have a few more. Just try your best to click it.

STUDENT: (Clicks here and there on the screen, missing the bandage) A box popped up with English words.

TUTOR: What do you think you should do next?

STUDENT: (Spends a lot of time staring at the English pop-up) Is this part of the learning material? (Gets stuck clicking on the unfamiliar English words instead of the bandage)

options.A: Disable unnecessary information about the inherent features of virtual objects, such as English system pop-up messages, so they do not appear on the screen.
options.B: Pair the student up with a new peer during the learning missions to help the new student learn to navigate through the 3D virtual health center.
options.C: Modify the learning missions assigned to the student to match their academic competence, and prefer oral rather than written responses when possible.
options.D: Compromise, negotiate situations, and share decisions and power with the student during the learning missions instead of imposing control.
